question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is **'across'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'looked out across' **makes sense as it implies an expansive view, encompassing the cityscape. It gives the connotation of viewing the city from a distance or a high vantage point, creating a visual stretch of the landscape.
 
• The use of **'across' **respects the sentence structure, enabling a smooth narrative flow. It maintains the coherence and overall flow of the sentence.
 
• **'Across' **is appropriate in this context as it denotes the action of viewing, visually scanning, or considering a wide area, in this case, the city.
 
• The word **'across' **enhances the descriptive nature of the narrative, providing sensory detail and aiding in the spatial understanding of the scene.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Outside: **This preposition suggests positioning or location exterior to a reference point. It doesn't give the expansive or panoramic view implied in the context.
 
• **Under: **This preposition indicates something beneath or lower than something else, which is not suitable in the context of looking out at a city.
 
• **Inside:** This preposition denotes something within a confined space, which doesn't make sense in this context as one cannot view the city looking out 'inside'.
